responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the SuperH (SH) family, covering the architecture-specific code generation, tuning, and operating-environment integration needed to compile for SH1 through SH4A and related subtargets. Its core is the hand-written backend logic and target configuration in sh.cc/sh.h together with the main machine description in sh.md, which define SH calling conventions, operand and address handling, prologue/epilogue generation, branch and delay-slot behavior, PIC/FDPIC support, T-bit and FPSCR/FPU state handling, instruction costs, and assembly emission. The surrounding .md families provide the declarative instruction ecosystem: predicates and constraints for legal RTL operands, shared iterators, atomic and synchronization patterns in sync.md, and per-core scheduling models for SH1, SH4, SH4A, and SH4-300. The module also includes SH-specific RTL optimization and memory-operation support passes, target option tables and C-family builtins/pragma handling, extra machine modes, and subtarget headers for ELF, Linux, NetBSD, RTEMS, VxWorks, newlib, and vendor-specific SuperH environments, plus build-time generators for SH division lookup tables used by runtime or code-generation support. Overall, this directory is responsible for translating GCC’s middle-end RTL into correct and tuned machine code for the many SH architectural variants and ABI/runtime combinations.
